nodes.title: Networking fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Networking moves packets between machines using layered protocols (the OSI / TCP-IP stack). Most exam questions test routing decisions, subnetting math, the difference between L2 and L3, and how DNS / DHCP make the whole thing usable for humans.

flashcards.front: What's the difference between Layer 2 and Layer 3?
flashcards.back: L2 (data link) uses MAC addresses to deliver frames inside a single broadcast domain (a switch). L3 (network) uses IP addresses to route packets between networks (a router). Switches do L2; routers do L3.

flashcards.front: How does a subnet mask work?
flashcards.back: The mask splits an IP into a network portion (the high bits, set to 1) and a host portion (the low bits, set to 0). `/24` means the first 24 bits are network = up to 256 hosts (254 usable). `/30` is 4 IPs = 2 hosts — typical for a point-to-point link.

Domain Name System translates human-readable names (`example.com`) into IP addresses. A recursive resolver asks the root, the TLD server (`.com`), and finally the authoritative server for the domain. TTL controls how long answers are cached.

flashcards.front: TCP vs UDP — when do you pick each?
flashcards.back: TCP is reliable, ordered, congestion-controlled — use it when every byte matters (HTTP, SSH, SMTP). UDP is lightweight, no handshake, no retransmit — use it for streaming, gaming, DNS queries, anywhere latency beats reliability.

nodes.title: Security fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Security is about layering defenses so no single failure compromises a system. Most exams test the same core ideas: least privilege, defense in depth, the CIA triad, and the shared-responsibility line between you and your cloud provider.

flashcards.back: Confidentiality (only the right people see the data), Integrity (data isn't tampered with), Availability (the system is reachable when needed). Every security control maps to at least one of these three pillars.
Grant each identity (user, role, service account) the minimum permissions needed to do its job — no more. The opposite is wildcard access, which makes a single credential leak catastrophic.
Stack multiple, independent controls so an attacker has to defeat all of them. Example: WAF in front of an app, network ACL on the subnet, IAM on the workload, encryption at rest in the database.

flashcards.front: Shared responsibility model — who does what?
flashcards.back: The cloud provider secures the cloud (physical hardware, hypervisor, region facilities). You secure what's IN the cloud (your data, IAM config, OS patching on EC2, application code). The exact line shifts by service: serverless is more on the provider, IaaS is more on you.

nodes.title: Part 4: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 4. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A team wants a CI pipeline that builds a Docker image, runs unit tests, scans for vulnerabilities, and pushes a signed image to Artifact Registry, triggered on every Git commit. What is the GCP-native implementation?
flashcards.back: Cloud Build is the GCP-native CI service. cloudbuild.yaml defines sequential steps: docker build, run tests, gcloud artifacts docker images scan, then sign the image. Cloud Build triggers fire automatically on repository events (push, PR). Cloud Build has native integration with Artifact Registry, Container Analysis, and Binary Authorization. test, scan, and sign steps; create a Cloud Build trigger linked to the source repository for automatic execution on commit

flashcards.front: A platform team manages GCP policies and Kubernetes configurations across 15 GKE clusters. They want a single Git repository as the source of truth with configurations automatically applied to all clusters. What capability enables this?
flashcards.back: Anthos Config Management (ACM) Config Sync: each cluster runs a Config Sync agent that continuously watches the Git repository. Any change to the repo is automatically applied to all registered clusters within seconds. Supports hierarchical configuration (root sync + namespace-level repo syncs). This is the GCP-native GitOps solution for multi-cluster management. which continuously reconciles cluster state from a Git repository supporting namespace and cluster-scoped configurations

flashcards.front: A GKE deployment was updated with a new container image that immediately started crashing. It has been failing for 5 minutes and must be rolled back to the last working version immediately. What is the fastest solution?
flashcards.back: kubectl rollout undo immediately restores the previous ReplicaSet (Kubernetes keeps rollout history). No Git commit, no CI/CD pipeline wait required. Kubernetes starts the old pods while terminating the new broken pods. This is the fastest recovery path. kubectl delete (option B) causes downtime during the gap between delete and re-apply.

flashcards.front: A developer needs to run a video transcoding job requiring 32GB RAM and up to 75 minutes to complete, triggered by Pub/Sub when new video files arrive in Cloud Storage. Which compute option supports these requirements?
flashcards.back: Cloud Run supports up to 32GB memory and 60-minute request timeout per request (as of 2024). Configure a Pub/Sub push subscription targeting the Cloud Run URL; each message triggers a transcoding job. Cloud Functions 2nd gen has a maximum 60-minute timeout but supports 32GB RAM. However, Cloud Run is the preferred choice for CPU-intensive, long-running container workloads. configure a Pub/Sub push subscription to trigger the Cloud Run service
